what: The register probe (this repository's EFI application) run on the handset: it printed the panel mode and eight EL1 registers, then held the screen

CNTFRQ_EL0.note: 19.2 MHz, matching the counter the loader reports

SCTLR_EL1.note: MMU and data cache on, instruction cache off at this point

TCR_EL1.note: matches the value the loader prints on its hand-off page

TTBR1_EL1.note: no high-half mapping before the loader installs one

reading: The machine looks ordinary at EL1: a Cortex-A53 r0p3, a 19.2 MHz counter, the firmware's identity tables, and the panel in the geometry the loader reported (1080x1920, 4320-byte rows, 32 bpp, base 0x400000).

Nothing here explains a kernel that stops before printing: the timer frequency is correct, the CPU is an A53 (the same architecture the emulator's cortex-a53 offers), the exception level is EL1 and TCR matches what the loader saw.

Because the kernel cannot print before arm_vm_init, the next instrument has to be inside the kernel: either a mapping for the framebuffer made from the kernel's own bootstrap page tables, or a check placed after the VM work and bisected backwards.
